name: Taupe
lede: Taupe is the French word for a mole, borrowed for a soft brownish grey; in the 1930s two teams of color standardizers found that the shade people called taupe was never quite the color of the animal.

sections.title: A mole's name
sections.body:
*Taupe* is the French word for a mole [1]. English borrowed it for a quiet, greyish brown[1]. Paterson's dictionary still lists mole as a shade of grey and sends the reader to taupe [2]. In the clothing trade, Paterson adds, [[beige]] is often renamed camel, taupe, [[stone]] or [[sand]] so that it does not sound like a color at all [5].

The swatch here is a warm, light-to-middling brownish grey, with more red than blue in it [3]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary dates the name in English to about 1850, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files this color in its block 23 [3].

sections.title: Chasing the mole
sections.body:
In 1932 the British Colour Council began a project to fix color names with dyed silk ribbons, hoping to do for color what the Oxford English Dictionary had done for words [1]. Maerz and Paul had already published their *Dictionary of Color* in New York in 1930, with pages of chips and an index of common names [1]. Both teams ran into the same problem with taupe: mole fur was agreed to be a deep grey on the cold side, but taupe was usually browner than any mole [1].

The Council guessed that English speakers simply did not know that taupe and mole were two words for one animal [1]. Maerz and Paul checked more thoroughly, visiting zoological museums in the United States and France to look at specimens of the mole genus *Talpa* [1]. They concluded that the fur varies, but that the color people meant by taupe was a considerable departure from any color a mole has, and they printed a sample matched to the average French mole instead [1].

St Clair adds that the effort failed to rein the word in: taupe has since stretched to cover a wide family of pale brown-greys, a roominess that makeup and bridal trades value for sounding refined [1]. The honest summary is that the name is stable and the color is not. Treat any taupe swatch, including this one, as one convention among several [1][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Taupe is one of the commonest named colors in our painting archive: it appears in 1,866 of 23,781 paintings, 7.85 per cent, and is more common than 91 per cent of the named colors [4]. The within-painting count, which asks whether the color is present as a distinct part of a picture, is 1,110 paintings [4].

The most devoted painters are not the ones you would guess from the word. Shen Zhou uses it in 7 of the 12 works we have, 3.7 times the museum baseline, while Vilhelm Hammershøi has it in 10 of 50, and [[painter:john-singer-sargent|Sargent]] in 22 of 287 [4]. Nepal is the most over-represented country, with 8 of 25 paintings [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays the hidden color, the one that sits quietly under the rest, in 35 per cent of the 1,110 paintings [4].

Three cautions apply. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and varnish browns everything, so a taupe match is not a pigment test [4]. Our earliest match, in the year 1000, is a floor set by a thin early archive, not a first [4]. And the English word itself peaks in the 1940s in printed books, close to when the standardizers were struggling with it [4].

questions.q: What does the word taupe mean in French?
What did Maerz and Paul conclude after looking at mole specimens in zoological museums?
choices: Taupe is a considerable departure from any color a mole has
Mole fur is a warm reddish brown
The two words name different animals
questions.answer: Taupe is a considerable departure from any color a mole has

questions.q: Mole fur was agreed to be a cold deep grey, while taupe is usually browner.

openers: Two teams of 1930s color standardizers visited zoological museums to check whether taupe really was the color of a mole; it was not.
Look for taupe as the quiet color under a picture: in our archive it is most often the hidden color, not the star.
